prompt: Build two evidence-based twelve-month roadmap variants from current authorized role descriptions: one for an operations-focused SRE/cloud role and one for an on-premises platform/private-cloud role. Use the canonical curriculum dependency graph, a bounded weekly capacity, learner-owned evidence, explicit gaps, production-shaped local projects, independent reviews and quarterly revision. Do not infer the learner's present level or hiring readiness.
directAnswer: Version both role inputs, translate requirements into durable capabilities and responsibility signals, and create one shared foundation plus role-specific branches. Inventory only authorized learner evidence and mark unknowns. Sequence milestones by dependency and risk, budget hours and reserve, define one useful artifact and failure/recovery exercise per milestone, and attach observable acceptance and reviewer ownership. Review monthly signals and make quarterly scope decisions. Keep role suitability, promotion and hiring outcomes outside the roadmap.
foundation: The strongest roadmap is not the longest. It minimizes dependency violations and produces evidence that can survive unfamiliar change. A shared Linux/networking/software/delivery/reliability foundation supports both paths; public cloud, private cloud, platform, data and architecture branches deepen only after their prerequisites have receipts.
reasoningSteps: Preserve each role source, date, stated level, operating context and unknowns.
Normalize title-specific wording into durable capabilities without erasing required vendor or environment knowledge.
Map capabilities to canonical curriculum IDs and prerequisite edges.
Record learner-owned observed, calculated, qualified, stale, prohibited and missing evidence.
Choose a shared foundation project that evolves rather than unrelated tutorial fragments.
Create branch milestones for AWS operations and for KVM/OpenStack/Ceph/OVS or equivalent private-cloud mechanisms.
Budget weekly focus, review, failure practice and recovery reserve; expose stopped work.
Define acceptance as artifact plus explanation plus changed-constraint recovery plus reviewer receipt.
Add interview and documentation practice only from truthful project evidence.
At each quarter, compare evidence to the role map and revise without auto-awarding a level.
seniorAnswer: I would use one versioned matrix with rows for role requirement, operation, state/failure mechanism, responsibility signal, curriculum prerequisite, current evidence, gap, milestone, artifact, fault, acceptance, reviewer and expiry. Months one through three would establish Linux, networking, Git, Bash/Python, tests and one observable service. Months four through six would add containers, CI/CD, IaC, telemetry, SLOs, incidents and recovery. The cloud branch would then model VPC/IAM/compute/storage/database/Kubernetes decisions locally and use current AWS task domains without creating resources. The private-cloud branch would deepen virtualization, image/network/storage control planes, Ceph-style failure, capacity and lifecycle using bounded local simulations. Both branches would include security, cost, documentation and leadership throughout. A maximum weekly budget would reserve time for review and recovery. Quarterly gates would require an unfamiliar reviewer-controlled failure and a concise architecture defense. Missing real production evidence would remain a gap, not be converted from the lab.
weakAnswer: Use the same roadmap for both roles, study one tool every week, and mark each skill complete after watching a course.
whyWeak: It ignores different operating contexts, dependencies, evidence strength, failure practice and sustainable capacity.

evidence.signal: Every milestone resolves to a canonical prerequisite and target-role requirement
evidence.proves: Roadmap traceability for the selected versions.
evidence.doesNotProve: The sequence is optimal for every learner or organization.

evidence.signal: Artifact, fault, recovery and reviewer receipt close a milestone
evidence.proves: Bounded observed practice and review occurred.

evidence.signal: Quarterly capacity ledger shows planned, completed, deferred and reserve hours
A changed target role produces a reviewed roadmap diff
evidence.proves: The plan adapts without erasing history.

followUps.prompt: How much weekly time should be planned?
followUps.answer: Use the learner's actual sustainable capacity, not a universal number. Reserve review and recovery time, then reduce scope when demand exceeds capacity.

followUps.prompt: Can one project cover many skills?
followUps.answer: Yes when each capability has distinct observable evidence and failure work. Do not double-count one successful deployment as proof of every surrounding domain.
After relevant foundation and practice, as optional versioned syllabus evidence. They may support screening but do not close production or responsibility gaps.

followUps.prompt: How should cloud learning remain local?
followUps.answer: Model APIs, state, IAM, networking, deployment and failure semantics with local fixtures and design exercises; label provider-runtime behavior unverified until authorized evidence exists.
When its declared artifact, explanation, independent changed-constraint exercise, cleanup and review receipt pass. Reading completion alone is not acceptance.

rubric.observableEvidence: Two versioned roles retain their different context, requirements and unknowns.
Tool wording becomes durable operations and mechanisms without dropping explicit requirements.
Learner-owned evidence classes, confidence, staleness, prohibitions and missing areas remain visible.
Shared foundation and specialist branches respect canonical prerequisites.
Each milestone has artifact, failure, recovery, explanation and observable acceptance.
Weekly limits, reserve, stopped work and revision rules are explicit.
Cloud-operations domains are covered locally without claiming provider-runtime evidence.
Virtualization, networking, storage, lifecycle and failure responsibilities receive distinct evidence.
Independent unfamiliar gates and delayed quarterly review control progression.
No inferred level, hiring prediction, fabricated evidence or course-equals-competence rule appears.
